answer: To keep an agent market from becoming an oasis for fake identities, its registry requires each identity to submit a fresh proof of work every epoch: find a nonce whose encryption under a public cipher key starts with 20 zero bits. Anyone can verify it with one encryption, but generating it takes about a million attempts on average. Each proof grants one vote for that epoch, so even an ember of influence must be renewed; a thousand fake agents cost roughly a billion attempts per epoch.
